items.stem: What is the key distinction between a code and a standard in ICT distribution design?

options.text: Codes are typically adopted law/mandatory; standards are often voluntary best-practice
options.rationale: Correct: codes carry the force of law when adopted, while many standards are voluntary consensus documents.

options.text: Standards are always legally mandatory and codes are optional
They mean exactly the same thing
options.rationale: They are distinct: enforceability and origin differ.

options.text: Neither has any bearing on design
options.rationale: Both codes and standards directly shape compliant design.

items.explanation: Correct: codes carry the force of law when adopted, while many standards are voluntary consensus documents.

items.stem: A proposed horizontal copper cabling run exceeds the recognised maximum channel length. What is the correct design response?

options.text: Redesign so the run stays within the recognised length limit (e.g. relocate the telecommunications room)
options.rationale: Correct: staying within recognised length limits is required to ensure performance and compliance.

options.text: Install it as-is and assume it will still pass
options.rationale: Exceeding limits risks failing performance requirements.
Grounding/bonding is a safety requirement, unrelated to and not a fix for length limits.

options.text: Use the exceeded length because fibre rules allow it
options.rationale: Fibre has different limits; they do not justify exceeding the copper channel limit.

items.explanation: Correct: staying within recognised length limits is required to ensure performance and compliance.

items.stem: Select TWO practices that support a well-coordinated ICT infrastructure design.

options.text: Coordinating pathways and spaces with mechanical, electrical and structural trades
options.rationale: Correct: multi-trade coordination avoids conflicts and rework.
Correct: coordinated, standards-referenced documentation supports correct installation and handover.

options.text: Designing in isolation from other building systems
options.rationale: Isolated design causes conflicts with other trades.

options.text: Omitting grounding and bonding to reduce cost
options.rationale: Grounding/bonding is a safety requirement and cannot be omitted.

options.text: Leaving length and fill limits undocumented
options.rationale: Undocumented limits lead to non-compliant installs.

items.explanation: Correct: multi-trade coordination avoids conflicts and rework.
